- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to counteract pessimism.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reverts to 1–2 week average of recent 10–15 day history; if model is drifting far from this, apply a “reversion bias” correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–2% to forecast if sentiment < 0.05 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead, not lagging 3–5 days.
